description: Canonical pathological contact dataset (TEST-02, issue #430). One reviewable manifest that every migration (MIG-*), import/export (DATA-*), round-trip (TEST-03), merge-golden (TEST-05) and performance (PERF-01) suite consumes instead of inventing its own thin fixture. Loader: backend/internal/canonicalfixture. See README.md.

contacts.name: ada
contacts.comment: trap #3: fields with no flat-column home (SpeakToAs, PersonalInfo, SocialProfiles, OtherOnlineServices, extra name components, Keywords, Notes, Localizations) must survive Record -> Contact -> Record via the neutral Card. RecordFromContact would silently drop all of it.

contacts.name: bob
contacts.comment: many repeatable fields (multiple emails/phones/addresses/orgs/titles), a photo media entry, a very long how_we_met and gender (the #515 round-trip hole is on crm.gender).

crm.how_we_met: Bob and I met at the accounting conference in 2003 — he was presenting the tax-policy talk and I was there for the CRM-data track, and we ended up sharing a table for lunch both days. We kept in touch through the annual meetups for a decade before he moved to Berlin and we started actually working together on the household budget work that eventually turned into a real project. The short version: conference lunch, two decades of birthdays, one shared spreadsheet. What follows is padding to get this column meaningfully long — close to the 1000-character ceiling the model validates — because long free-text fields are a separate failure class: a how_we_met that is fine at two hundred characters can silently truncate, mangle, or fail to round-trip at eight hundred, and this contact is the regression net for that. He answers every email within a day, keeps the shared files organised, and knows the exact date of everything.

contacts.name: test07_empty_note_with_params
contacts.comment: TEST-07 (issue #435) shrunk counterexample, persisted: a note with empty text but a CREATED param. vCard 3.0 dropped the param without the required warn because the empty note was skipped before the warn fired; the round-trip property found it and the vcard3 adapter now warns.

contacts.name: test07_timestamped_birthday
contacts.comment: TEST-07 (issue #435) shrunk counterexample, persisted: a birthday with a full timestamp. vCard 3.0 renders BDAY date-only and dropped the time-of-day without a warn; the round-trip property found it and the vcard3 adapter now warns.

contacts.name: test07_country_code_only_address
contacts.comment: TEST-07 (issue #435) shrunk counterexample, persisted: an address carrying only a country code. vCard 3.0 has no ADR CC parameter and the required warn never fired because the address was skipped as empty; the round-trip property found it and the vcard3 adapter now warns before the skip.

contacts.name: test07_multi_grammatical_gender
contacts.comment: TEST-07 (issue #435) shrunk counterexample, persisted: two grammatical genders. JSContact's scalar speakToAs.grammaticalGender collapsed them without a warn; the round-trip property found it and the jscontact adapter now warns.

contacts.name: test07_duplicate_keywords
contacts.comment: TEST-07 (issue #435) shrunk counterexample, persisted: duplicate keywords. JSContact's boolean-set keywords collapsed them without a warn; the round-trip property found it and the jscontact adapter now warns. The keywords were once the NFD spelling e+U+0301tude; I18N-02 (issue #485) canonicalizes stored text to NFC on write, so the corpus carries the canonical spelling and the NFD-variant round-trip is covered by the normalize tests (contactmodel/normalize_test.go).

notes.content: Ada prefers written correspondence. Always reply within a day.

Bob's file predates the CRM and arrived via the old CSV import, which means every field was flattened and then re-expanded — so this note carries the history of that migration: the original row had three employers, two addresses, and a phone number written five different ways across five years of exports, and the import merge reconciled them into the current record. The import tool wrote its audit trail here: it kept the first employer as primary because the second address stopped being valid after the 2018 move; it resolved the phone-number country-code discrepancy in favour of the +49 value over the 0049 spelling because the latter only ever appeared in the old export format; and it merged three email addresses by de-duplicating the two that differed only by a trailing dot. This note is deliberately long because long notes are a separate failure class: a text column that is fine at 200 characters can silently truncate, mangle, or fail to round-trip at 2000, and this contact is the regression net for exactly that. The length also exercises the FTS tokenizer against a single large field rather than many small ones, which is a different query plan. Past the two-thousand-character mark the content itself no longer matters; what matters is that every character — the umlauts, the em dashes, the digits, the trailing punctuation, and the repeated long words that a truncating implementation would cut in half — survives a save, a migration, an export, and a re-import byte for byte. A truncation would also be visible in the raw byte count, which is why the suite that consumes this fixture checks the length of this exact field rather than trusting the round trip alone.
